sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Windows-only Outlook package
sections.what: Adds pywin32, which lets the app control the Windows Outlook program to send email.
sections.why: Likely reason: sending email through Outlook needs Windows automation.
sections.watch_out: pywin32 installs only on Windows, so a plain pip install on Linux or macOS fails at this line.

summary: A list of the Python packages the backend needs, with minimum versions.
purpose: Tells pip which packages to install so the backend can run.
why: Lets one install command set up everything the backend uses.
how: pip reads each line in order and installs the named package at or above the given version. Comments are ignored. Lines are grouped by purpose: web server, language model tools, vector store, document readers, email, SharePoint, Azure, OCR, utilities, data handling, logging and testing.
inputs: The package names and minimum versions listed in the file.
outputs: Installed packages in the Python environment, which may be newer than the minimums.
risks: Minimum-only pins let fresh installs pull newer versions that change behaviour. The pywin32 line installs only on Windows, so installation fails on Linux and macOS. The pypff line is commented out because it is not available on newer Python versions.
debug: If installation fails, look for the pywin32 line first if you are not on Windows. Check the Python version against the one the packages support. Run the install again in a fresh environment to see the first error.
